Consult Summary:
- Teleconsult for sudden-onset left-sided headache with visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting and dizziness; clinician impression: migraine; advised ibuprofen plus anti-sickness medication and sugary carbonated drink; same-day in-person neurological assessment planned with option to cancel if symptoms resolve.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided headache with visual symptoms.
- Onset/duration: Began this morning; approximately 4 hours before the consult; sudden onset.
- Severity: 6/10 (patient compares 10/10 to prior kidney stone pain).
- Character/location: Unilateral (left side); not clearly behind the eye.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Visual: Blurred vision with zigzag lines.
  - Nausea with two episodes of vomiting at onset; ongoing nausea.
  - Dizziness.
  - Screen intolerance; feels worse with movement; prefers head kept still.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No limb weakness reported.
  - Able to walk in a straight line; gait not affected per patient.
- Exacerbating factors: Movement; using screens.
- Relieving factors: Keeping head still (patient preference; benefit not explicitly stated).
- Prior treatments: Paracetamol taken ~3 hours after onset (dose/route/frequency not documented) with no relief.
- Similar episodes: None; first episode of this type.
- Pregnancy: Patient states pregnancy is unlikely.

Past Medical History:
- Nephrolithiasis (kidney stones) in the past.
- Other medical problems: Patient initially said “yes,” then clarified “not actually” (conflict noted).
- Medications: No regular medications reported.
- Drug allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Not discussed.

Family History:
- Mother with migraines.
- Hypothyroidism in the family; mother reported to have hypothyroidism.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical exam performed during this teleconsult.

Investigations:
- None discussed or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache with visual disturbance and nausea/vomiting – likely migraine (with visual aura).
  - Advise trial of ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Add an anti-sickness medication obtainable from pharmacy (specific agent not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Encourage sugary, carbonated beverage (e.g., cola).
  - Arrange same-day in-person evaluation for a full neurological examination.
  - If medications are effective and patient feels much better before the appointment, patient may call to cancel.
  - If symptoms persist or worsen before the appointment, contact the clinic.
- Issue 2: Nausea and vomiting secondary to headache.
  - Use antiemetic as above (OTC per pharmacy advice; specifics not documented).
  - Maintain oral intake with fluids; include sugary carbonated drink as advised.
- Issue 3: Health anxiety regarding stroke/brain tumor.
  - Provided education that features (unilateral headache, visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting) are typical of migraine.
  - Noted that migraine onset can occur at various ages.
  - Plan for in-person neuro exam to further assess and reassure.

General plan items:
- None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs; full neurological exam; comprehensive red flag screen (e.g., fever, neck stiffness, worst-ever “thunderclap,” head/neck trauma, anticoagulation use); medication doses/routes/frequencies; pregnancy testing/LMP; social history (smoking, alcohol, substances); complete medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: Patient initially endorsed other medical problems, then stated “not actually” (conflict noted). Clinician repeated “hyperthyroid,” patient clarified family history is hypothyroidism.
- Transcript quality: Minor connectivity issues and brief interruptions; overall adequate to determine key clinical details.
